app.name: RepoBuddy
app.tagline: AI assistant for understanding codebases via knowledge graphs

nav.quotaTitle: Your daily usage. Admins and BYOK users bypass enforcement.

interest.title: Tell the team you'd use higher limits
interest.modalBody: We're still figuring out whether to introduce paid plans. A click here tells us there's demand — and an optional note helps prioritise what you actually need (more workspaces? bigger token budget? team plan?). One submission per account.
interest.messagePlaceholder: e.g. I'd pay $5/mo for 10× more tokens / unlimited workspaces / etc.

s1.title: Ask anything — get cited answers
s1.body: Type a question. Every claim in the answer carries a clickable citation (↗ opens the source, ◆ opens the entity's neighbour graph).

s2.title: Reasoning is transparent
s2.body: The Reasoning panel on the right shows the plan the AI ran — find_symbol → get_callers → answer. Click a step to inspect its result.

s3.title: Explore the codebase
s3.body: Explore (top right) opens a treemap of every file, sized by LOC and coloured by hotness or coverage. Click a tile to dive into that file's neighbour graph.

admin.title: Admin
admin.subtitle: Service-wide observability and bulk actions. Visible to GitHub logins listed in ADMIN_LOGINS.

interest.empty: No one has tapped "Want more?" yet. The button shows in the header for users who haven't bypass status.

cards.weekHint: sum of all phases × all workspaces

overview.intro: For graphs use Grafana. This page is the operator's quick-glance.

admin.bulkDeleteBody: This permanently removes the selected workspaces, including their graphs, chunks and chats. Cannot be undone.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Configure your own LLM endpoint so the server doesn't charge against the shared quota.
settings.byokHelp: Point RepoBuddy at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, Together, Ollama, vLLM…). When configured, your requests bypass the daily token limit because you're paying your own bill.
settings.baseUrlHint: Default is https://api.openai.com/v1. Use Groq: https://api.groq.com/openai/v1, OpenRouter: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, Ollama: http://localhost:11434/v1.
settings.apiKeyHint: Encrypted at rest. Leave blank to keep the existing key.
settings.cleared: BYOK cleared. Server defaults will be used.
settings.clearConfirmBody: Server defaults will be used after this. You can paste the key again later.

hero.title: Your first PR to any open-source repo. Faster.
hero.subtitle: RepoBuddy indexes a project into a knowledge graph, then shows you what runs, what matters, and where a safe first contribution could land — so you stop bouncing off unfamiliar codebases.
hero.cta2: Already have an account? Open dashboard

0.title: Get oriented in minutes
0.body: The contributor's tour surfaces entry points, the classes and functions everything depends on, and small stable files safe for a first PR — derived from the graph, not the README.

1.title: Pick up real issues
1.body: Open GitHub issues tagged good-first-issue / help-wanted are linked back to the code they touch and ranked by how much surface area they cover.

2.title: Run it locally on the first try
2.body: Setup commands auto-extracted from package.json, Makefile, Dockerfile and the README's Quick Start section. One click to copy.

3.title: Follow a flow as a diagram
3.body: Walkthrough turns a function or route into a Mermaid sequence diagram of its actual call chain — so a 12-step transaction reads in 30 seconds.

4.title: Ask anything, get cited answers
4.body: Each claim links to a specific chunk or entity. A KAG planner stitches multi-hop reasoning (find_symbol → get_callers → answer) and shows the plan + trace inline.

5.title: Judge project health at a glance
5.body: Hotness, active maintainers, fix-to-feat ratio, bus factor, breaking-change frequency — so you know if the project is worth contributing to before you sink hours.

public.title: Try it on a project you might contribute to
public.subtitle: These workspaces are open to anyone — open the tour, ask questions, skim the issues. No account needed.

languages.title: Supported languages
languages.subtitle: Static analysis covers four languages today. Markdown and per-commit diffs are indexed for every repo regardless of language.

workspace.reindexConfirmBody: We'll re-clone the repo, re-parse files, re-annotate with the LLM and re-embed chunks. This costs tokens (typically $0.20–$2 depending on repo size) and replaces the existing graph. Worth doing after the source repo gets new commits or you change the active model.
workspace.deleteConfirmBody: This permanently removes the workspace, its graph, chunks, embeddings, and all chats. To confirm, type the workspace name: {name}
workspace.publicHint: Anyone with the link can open this workspace in read-only mode (chat with guest limits, graph). No reindex / delete / settings.
